candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.8, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Promote staff and workplace safety; Protect clients and healthcare personnel from environmental hazards; Follow safety procedures
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — workplace-violence reporting and prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize reporting and recordkeeping of threats, aggressive behavior, close calls, and violent incidents as tools for workplace-hazard detection, trend analysis, and violence-prevention improvement.

options.A: Because verbal threats should be excluded from documentation so the facility's workplace-safety statistics are not affected.
options.B: Because only incidents causing a recordable physical injury provide useful information for a workplace-violence prevention program.
options.C: Because reports and near-miss records help identify patterns and hazards, support investigation and risk assessment, and guide prevention and program improvement.
options.D: Because incident records are unrelated to prevention; workplace-violence programs depend only on the number of security staff assigned.

candidate.rationale: OSHA's hospital workplace-violence eTool encourages prompt reporting of all violent incidents and describes recordkeeping and program evaluation as core prevention-program components. OSHA specifically identifies near-miss reports of verbal attacks or aggressive behavior and explains that records can reveal trends and patterns, evaluate hazard controls, identify training needs, and support solutions. C is therefore correct. A, B, and D would remove information OSHA identifies as important to prevention.
candidate.source_claim_supported: OSHA encourages prompt reporting of violent incidents, threats and close calls; recordkeeping helps identify trends, assess hazards and controls, and improve workplace-violence prevention programs.
candidate.source_document_title: Hospitals eTool — Hospital-wide Hazards — Workplace Violence
